To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Texas basement records more than 200 m.y. of Mesoproterozoicoic arc-continent and collisional orogenesis culminating in the assembly of Rodina.

(1) the Texas basement contains the southern margin of the Laurentian continent during the assembly of the Mesoproterozoicoic supercontinent of Rodinia; (2) the Texas basement records a complex history of arc-continent and possibly continent-continent collision culminating in ca. 1155–1120 Ma orogeny; (3) the Texas basement is a critical part of the southern Laurentia margin during the assembly and breakup of Rodinia; and (4) the Texas basement

the Grenville orogenic event along the southern margin Laurentia was initiated ca. 1380 Ma by collision between Laurentia and the Archean Yavapai province, and that the orogen grew southward as Laurentia collided with a 1320–1280 Ma island arc and the 1250–1200 Ma cratonic margin of the Minto block, which was accreted during the 1250-1120 Ma Grenville event.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(1) the tectonic and stratigraphic evolution of the southern margin of the North American craton; and (2) the tectonostratigraphic evolution and geodynamic setting of the southern Grenville orogenic system.
the tectonic history of the southern margin of the North American craton, and the evolution of the Grenville orogenic system.
the tectonic history of the southern Laurentia margin and how this relates to the evolution of the supercontinent Rodinia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Texas basement represents an arc-continent collisional orogen that formed along the southern Laurentian craton during the Mesoproterozoicoic and that this collisional orogen is a component of the Grenville orogenic event.
the Grenville orogenic system is a classic example of an arc-continent collisional system, and the Texas basement provides the best exposure of this collisional system.

the Texas basement records a Mesoproterozoicoic history of subduction, arc-continent collision, and continent-continent collisions along a passive margin that was ultimately transformed into a convergent margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Texas basement is a collage of exotic island arc, backarc basin, and Laurentian continental crust that was assembled along the southern margin during Mesoprozoic time.
the Grenville orogenic system is a classic example of a continental collision zone that records the assembly of Rodinian continental blocks and their amalgamation to form Laurentia.
the Texas Grenville orogen is an arc-continent collisional orogen, and that the orogenic history of this region is similar to the Canadian Grenville.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Texas basement is a key part of the southern Laurentia margin during the Mesoproterozoicoic, not a backarc of the Laurentian margin.
the southern Laurentian orogen was a collage of exotic terranes accreted to Laurentia during the assembly of the supercontinent Rodinia.
a continental margin is a dynamic, evolving system.
